questions.text: The slope of the Capital Market Line equals:
options: Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio
questions.explanation: The slope of the CML is the Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio, representing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: A 'risk-neutral' investor:
options: Demands the highest risk premium for all investments
Focuses only on expected return, ignoring risk
questions.explanation: A risk-neutral investor evaluates investments solely on expected returns without regard for risk.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: Creating a household budget helps primarily to:
options: Identify surplus or deficit and control spending
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps monitor expenses and ensures planned savings.

questions.text: Which of these is the least expensive form of credit?
questions.explanation: Gold loan is secured and typically has lower interest than unsecured credit.

questions.text: Which expense would be classified as discretionary?
questions.explanation: Dining out is non-essential and discretionary in nature.

questions.text: NRIs investing in Indian mutual funds must comply with:
questions.explanation: NRI investments are governed by FEMA and RBI rules for inward and outward remittances.

questions.text: The best way to monitor whether a family is living within its means is to:
options: Compare total expenses with after-tax income regularly
questions.explanation: Comparing expenses with income ensures sustainability.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of mis-selling?
options: Explaining all risks clearly before sale
Selling a product unsuitable for the client’s risk profile to earn higher commission
questions.explanation: Mis-selling includes pushing unsuitable products mainly to earn higher commissions, ignoring client needs and risk profile.

questions.text: SEBI mandates that investor complaints and their resolution status must be:
options: Displayed on AMC and intermediary websites
Submitted only to the Ministry of Finance
questions.explanation: Transparency requires intermediaries to disclose complaint numbers and status on their websites.

questions.text: Which of these improves the current ratio (liquid assets ÷ current liabilities)?
questions.explanation: Reducing liabilities with existing cash improves ratio.

questions.text: An AIF may be set up as a trust, company, LLP or:
questions.explanation: AIFs can be established as a trust, company, limited-liability partnership or body corporate.

questions.text: A stock split means:
options: Company merges two shares into one
Company divides each share into smaller units to increase liquidity
Company issues new shares for cash
questions.explanation: A stock split divides shares into smaller units to make them more affordable and increase liquidity.

questions.text: Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) must invest at least how much of their portfolio in equity securities?
questions.explanation: ELSS schemes must hold at least 80% of their portfolio in equity securities and offer tax deduction under Section 80C under the old tax regime.

questions.text: Which SEBI regulation governs Alternate Investment Funds (AIFs)?
questions.explanation: AIFs are governed under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.

questions.text: A liquidity ratio of 6 indicates that:
options: Liquid assets can cover 6 months of expenses
questions.explanation: It means the person can survive 6 months without new income.

questions.text: The minimum net worth requirement for Portfolio Managers is:
questions.explanation: Under SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: The financial life cycle typically starts with which stage?
questions.explanation: The financial life cycle begins when an individual starts earning and accumulating assets.

questions.text: The coefficient of correlation between portfolio and market returns is denoted by:
questions.explanation: ρ (rho) represents the correlation coefficient between two variables—in this case, portfolio and market returns.

questions.text: Which of the following is typically classified as a REAL asset rather than a financial asset?
questions.explanation: Real estate is a tangible real asset, while FDs, equity and bonds are financial assets.

questions.text: Advisory Portfolio Management Services are primarily meant for:
questions.explanation: In advisory PMS, the manager only provides investment ideas or guidance, typically for institutional clients who execute trades themselves.

questions.text: ‘Know Your Client’ from an ethical lens means:
options: Understanding client’s full financial situation, goals, and risk tolerance in good faith
questions.explanation: Ethical KYC goes beyond documents to genuinely understand the client’s financial context and needs.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, investor complaints must be redressed within:
questions.explanation: Intermediaries are expected to resolve investor grievances within 30 days of receipt.

questions.text: Money-weighted rate of return is also known as:
questions.explanation: Money-weighted return is the internal rate of return (IRR) that equates the present value of cash inflows and outflows.

questions.text: Which of the following investors typically dominate the institutional segment?
options: Mutual funds, insurance companies, pension funds and FPIs
questions.explanation: Institutional segment comprises entities like mutual funds, insurers, pension funds and foreign portfolio investors.

questions.text: Which statement about diversification is correct in personal finance?
options: It spreads investments across different assets to reduce unsystematic risk
questions.explanation: Diversification helps reduce unsystematic risk by spreading investments, but it cannot eliminate market risk.

questions.text: The minimum corpus for each AIF scheme must be at least:
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹50 crore, while angel funds have relaxed limits.

questions.text: Jensen’s Alpha represents:
options: The difference between actual and CAPM-expected return
The slope of the Security Market Line
questions.explanation: Jensen’s Alpha = Actual Return – [Risk-Free Rate + β × (Market Return – Risk-Free Rate)], measuring excess return over CAPM.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT typically part of personal financial planning?
options: Determining the monetary policy of the country
questions.explanation: Monetary policy is handled by the central bank, not part of individual financial planning.

questions.text: The formula for the Sharpe Ratio is:
options: (Portfolio Return – Risk-Free Rate) / Standard Deviation of Portfolio
questions.explanation: Sharpe Ratio = (Rp – Rf) / σp, where Rp is portfolio return, Rf is risk-free rate, and σp is portfolio’s standard deviation.

questions.text: The minimum net worth requirement for an Investment Adviser (non-individual) is:
questions.explanation: Non-individual Investment Advisers must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹25 lakh as per SEBI (IA) Regulations.

questions.text: Which one of these reduces total interest cost on a loan?
options: Making part prepayments early in the tenure
questions.explanation: Early prepayments reduce outstanding principal faster, saving interest.

questions.text: Category III AIFs must maintain leverage within limits specified by:
questions.explanation: SEBI specifies limits and disclosure norms for leverage taken by Category III AIFs.

questions.text: The primary objective of SEBI is to:
options: Protect investor interests and regulate the securities market
questions.explanation: SEBI’s core objectives are investor protection, market regulation, and development of the securities market.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a securities market participant?
questions.explanation: Registrar of Companies handles company registration and filings, not market trading.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the payoff for a call option buyer?
options: Unlimited profit potential, limited loss (premium paid)
questions.explanation: A call buyer’s loss is limited to the premium, while potential profit is theoretically unlimited.

questions.text: For arbitration of disputes between investors and brokers, the forum used is:
questions.explanation: Exchange arbitration panels handle disputes between investors and brokers as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

questions.text: Which is the MOST suitable investment for parking an emergency fund?
options: Liquid mutual fund or savings bank account
questions.explanation: Emergency funds must be readily accessible and low risk, so liquid funds or savings accounts are appropriate.

questions.text: Minimum net worth required for registration of a Portfolio Manager under SEBI (2020) Regulations is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: An intermediary found guilty of mis-selling or misconduct may face:
options: Suspension or cancellation of registration by SEBI
Tax penalty by Income Tax Department
questions.explanation: SEBI can suspend, cancel, or impose monetary penalties on intermediaries violating regulations.

questions.text: Transmission of mutual fund units occurs when:
options: Investor wants to transfer to a friend
Investor dies and legal heir claims ownership
questions.explanation: Transmission refers to the transfer of ownership of mutual fund units to legal heirs or nominees upon death of the holder.

questions.text: PFRDA regulates:
options: National Pension System (NPS) and specified pension schemes
questions.explanation: PFRDA oversees NPS and other pension schemes under its jurisdiction.

questions.text: The 'consolidation phase' in the investor life cycle is typically when:
options: Income exceeds expenses and focus shifts to capital preservation
The investor depends entirely on investment income
The investor is gifting wealth to heirs
questions.explanation: In the consolidation phase, income exceeds expenses, and investors begin emphasizing capital preservation.

questions.text: SEBI’s role in the equity market is to:
options: Regulate issuers and intermediaries, and protect investor interests
Fix the price of every stock
Act as a broker for retail investors
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates markets and intermediaries to ensure fair practices and investor protection.

questions.text: Inflation risk refers to the risk that:
options: An issuer will default on payments
Market prices will be volatile in the short term
Purchasing power of money will erode over time
questions.explanation: Inflation risk is the risk that rising prices reduce the real value of investment returns.

questions.text: Which document must a PMS provide to clients before onboarding?
questions.explanation: The PMS must furnish a Disclosure Document detailing fees, risks, related-party transactions, and performance.

questions.text: A normal (upward sloping) yield curve typically indicates that:
options: Short-term rates are higher than long-term rates
Investors demand higher yields for longer maturities
There is no difference in yields across maturities
The economy is always in recession
questions.explanation: In a normal yield curve, longer maturities carry higher yields as compensation for higher time and liquidity risk.

questions.text: Sector funds must invest at least what percentage of total assets in the identified sector?
questions.explanation: Open-ended sector funds must invest at least 80% of total assets in equity and equity-related instruments of the specified sector.

questions.text: A stock with beta greater than 1 is expected to:
options: Be less volatile than the market
Move in opposite direction to market
Be more volatile than the market
questions.explanation: A beta > 1 indicates higher volatility compared to market movements.

questions.text: Category I AIFs generally invest in:
questions.explanation: Category I AIFs include venture-capital, SME, social-venture and infrastructure funds that create positive economic impact.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a typical money market instrument in India?
questions.explanation: A 10-year G-Sec is a long-term dated security; the others are classic money market instruments with maturities up to one year.

questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: A mutual fund investment can be made through which of the following modes?
options: Cheque, demand draft, electronic transfer, or UPI
questions.explanation: Investors can invest using cheque, DD, NEFT/RTGS, or digital modes such as UPI or net banking.

questions.text: A mutual fund is best described as:
options: A bank account where money is kept only in cash
An investment vehicle that pools money from investors to invest in a portfolio of securities
A company that gives fixed deposits with guaranteed returns
A government savings scheme with fixed interest
questions.explanation: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in a portfolio of securities such as equity, debt or gold, managed by an AMC.

questions.text: Banking-related complaints are addressed by:
questions.explanation: The RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme handles grievances related to banks and NBFCs.

questions.text: A change in mode of holding (single to joint) in a mutual fund folio:
options: Is allowed with consent of all parties
Is not permitted; a new folio must be created
questions.explanation: Change in mode of holding is not allowed in existing folios; a new folio must be created with the new configuration.

questions.text: Find the present value of ₹50,000 receivable after 5 years at 9% p.a. compounded annually.
Time value of an option refers to:
options: The coupon paid over the life of the option
The difference between option premium and its intrinsic value
questions.explanation: Time value represents the premium component attributable to the time left till expiry and expected volatility.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a category of AIF under SEBI regulations?
questions.explanation: There are only three categories of AIF — Category I, II and III.

questions.text: The main advantage of secured loans over unsecured loans is:
options: Lower interest rates due to collateral
questions.explanation: Collateral reduces lender’s risk, allowing lower interest rates.

questions.text: Liquidity in the stock market means:
options: Ability to trade shares quickly without major price change
questions.explanation: Liquidity allows quick trade execution at stable prices.

questions.text: Advertising by SEBI-registered intermediaries must be:
options: Factually correct, fair, and not misleading
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that advertisements must be true, fair, and not misleading, and must include risk disclosures.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the term financial independence?
options: Having sufficient assets and income sources to maintain desired lifestyle without active employment
questions.explanation: Financial independence means being able to meet living expenses from investments and passive income without needing to work.

questions.text: Holders of equity shares are known as:
questions.explanation: Equity shareholders are owners and have residual claims on assets and profits.

questions.text: In a conservative hybrid fund, the typical allocation to debt and equity is:
questions.explanation: Conservative hybrid funds predominantly invest in debt (75–90%) with a small equity allocation of 10–25%.

questions.text: Which budgeting method allocates funds first to essential expenses and savings before discretionary spending?
questions.explanation: Pay-yourself-first ensures savings are prioritised before optional spending.

questions.text: Stock brokers are required to be:
options: Registered with and regulated by SEBI and the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Brokers are SEBI-registered intermediaries and also members of stock exchanges.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: Distressed securities typically refer to:
options: Securities of issuers facing financial difficulty or near default
Government securities with high credit rating
questions.explanation: Distressed securities are issued by companies in financial distress, often trading at deep discounts due to high perceived risk.

questions.text: The foreign exchange market in India consists of:
options: Spot, forward and exchange-traded currency derivatives segments
questions.explanation: India has spot, forward and exchange-traded currency derivatives markets.

questions.text: If a perpetuity pays ₹1,000 per year and the discount rate is 8%, the present value is:
questions.explanation: PV = 1,000 / 0.08 = 12,500 → closest ₹10,000 ? Wait check: 1,000/0.08 = 12,500 = Option A?** actually 12,500**, adjust to A.

questions.text: The Information Ratio evaluates:
options: Excess return relative to benchmark divided by total risk
Excess return relative to benchmark divided by tracking error
Total portfolio return divided by benchmark return
questions.explanation: Information Ratio = (Rp – Rb) / Tracking Error, measuring the manager’s ability to generate active return consistently.

questions.text: Coupon yield is defined as:
options: Annual coupon divided by market price
Annual coupon divided by face value
Face value divided by market price
Market price divided by annual coupon
questions.explanation: Coupon yield = coupon payment / face value; it is the nominal coupon rate printed on the bond.

questions.text: The ‘hurdle rate’ in a PMS refers to:
options: The minimum return required before profit-sharing fees apply
questions.explanation: The hurdle rate is the minimum return the PMS must achieve before charging performance fees.

questions.text: A bond trades at a premium to face value when:
options: Coupon rate is equal to the current market yield
Coupon rate is higher than the current market yield
Coupon rate is lower than the current market yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon exceeds the market yield, investors are willing to pay more than face value, so the bond trades at a premium.

questions.text: Which type of goal is "funding daughter’s marriage" usually considered as?
questions.explanation: Spending on major life events such as marriage is a consumption goal because it relates to a one-time use of funds.

questions.text: Which of the following are the main segments of the Indian debt market?
options: Government securities, PSU and bank bonds, and corporate debt instruments
Only government securities and equity shares
Only treasury bills and commercial papers
Corporate equity, real estate and commodities
questions.explanation: The Indian debt market broadly comprises government securities (G-Secs and SDLs), PSU/bank bonds and private sector corporate debt instruments.

questions.text: Rights issue means:
options: Issue of shares to new investors
Issue of shares to existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings
questions.explanation: A rights issue offers additional shares to existing shareholders in proportion to their current holdings.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes ‘Direct Access Facility’ in PMS?
options: A service allowing investors to transact through distributors
A feature enabling investors to invest directly without intermediaries
A regulatory exemption from SEBI registration
A facility allowing mutual fund investors to switch to PMS
questions.explanation: Under the direct access facility, investors can invest directly in PMS without intermediaries, reducing cost.

questions.text: Stock market indices such as Nifty 50 or Sensex are designed to:
questions.explanation: Stock indices serve as barometers of market performance.

questions.text: Why is inflation an important factor in financial planning?
options: It increases the nominal value of assets automatically
It reduces the purchasing power of money over time
questions.explanation: Inflation erodes purchasing power; therefore, goals must be planned in inflation-adjusted terms.

questions.text: Preferred shareholders generally have:
options: Priority over equity shareholders in dividend and liquidation but limited voting rights
Higher returns than equity in all circumstances
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders get fixed dividends and priority in liquidation but limited or no voting rights.

questions.text: An individual’s income: ₹80,000, EMIs: ₹20,000, other fixed expenses: ₹30,000, variable: ₹20,000. What’s savings ratio?
questions.explanation: Savings = 80 − (20+30+20)=10; 10/80=12.5%? Correct index 1 actually.

questions.text: SWP (Systematic Withdrawal Plan) is typically used by investors to:
options: Withdraw a fixed sum regularly from existing investments
questions.explanation: SWP enables investors to withdraw a fixed amount at regular intervals from their investment corpus.

questions.text: If the Sharpe Ratio of a portfolio is less than that of the market, it indicates:
options: Portfolio underperforms on a risk-adjusted basis
questions.explanation: A lower Sharpe Ratio than the market indicates inferior risk-adjusted performance.

questions.text: One key benefit of having a written financial plan is that it:
options: Helps in clarifying priorities and tracking progress toward goals
Ensures there will be no market risk
questions.explanation: A written plan helps organise goals, prioritise them and monitor progress objectively over time.

questions.text: Liquidity risk is BEST described as the risk that:
options: Investor cannot sell the investment quickly at a fair price
questions.explanation: Liquidity risk is the risk of not being able to exit an investment promptly at a reasonable price.

questions.text: In an EMI, the interest component:
options: Is zero in the first year
questions.explanation: As principal outstanding reduces, the interest portion of each EMI declines.

questions.text: If two assets are perfectly positively correlated, diversification will:
options: Have no effect on portfolio risk
questions.explanation: Perfect positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +1) means both assets move identically, offering no diversification benefit.

questions.text: An emergency fund should be kept mainly in:
questions.explanation: Liquidity and safety are priorities for emergency funds.

questions.case_text: Manoj has a home loan of ₹40 lakh at 8.5% p.a. for 20 years. His EMI is ₹34,700. He also has a personal loan of ₹5 lakh at 12% for 3 years. Monthly income ₹1 lakh.

questions.text: Total EMI burden per month (approx.):
questions.explanation: Personal-loan EMI ≈ 17 k → total ≈ 52 k.

questions.text: DTI ratio is roughly:
questions.explanation: 52 k ÷ 1 lakh = 52%. High → risky.

questions.text: To reduce DTI, Manoj should first:
questions.explanation: Personal loan has high rate; clearing it cuts DTI fast.

questions.text: Which loan is secured?
questions.explanation: Home loan is secured by property.

questions.text: If interest falls to 7.5% p.a., EMI reduces by about:
questions.explanation: Roughly ₹1 k drop per lakh interest cut on long-term loan.

questions.case_text: Rohit wants to buy a car costing ₹12 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year loan at 10% p.a. interest. He can pay the full price from his savings or take the loan and invest his money in a debt mutual fund earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: Loan interest rate offered is:

questions.case_text: Ajay, aged 45, wants to retire at 60. His current monthly expenses are ₹70,000, expected to rise by 6% annually. He expects 7% post-retirement returns and plans to live till 85. Inflation-adjusted corpus required is to be estimated.

questions.case_text: Meena invests ₹20,000 per month for 15 years in an equity SIP giving 12% p.a. compounded monthly. Inflation averages 5%.

questions.text: Approximate future corpus?
Real (inflation-adjusted) corpus value is roughly:
questions.explanation: Real ≈ Nominal ÷ (1.05)^15 ≈ 65 lakh.

questions.text: Her investment pattern is an example of:
questions.explanation: Regular monthly SIPs are an annuity-type investment.

questions.text: If returns fall to 10%, corpus will approximately be:

questions.text: Key learning from this caselet:
questions.explanation: Discipline and compounding over time generate substantial corpus.
